answer: Increasing-cost identity slots.** Each new identity must rent a slot priced by a convex curve on the current active count, so marginal cost rises for every replica an attacker adds. At low counts the fee is trivial, letting organic adoption spread like a willow; near the system zenith, each extra identity costs exponentially more. Honest users fund slots from garden-variety transaction revenue, but a sybil farm must pay the steep tail repeatedly, making mass fabrication economically self-defeating.
